rationale: Clean beat ($8.81 vs $8.63), strong execution: revenue $3.21B above guidance, record FCF $1.066B, advanced packaging revenue up ~70% YoY to $925M+ creating a new $11B SAM. Management says customer 'body language' indicates urgency to secure slots. 2026 guided to be growth year with broader spending profile, first half flat-to-modestly-up and 'accelerating growth in second half.' Dec Q guide $3.225B roughly in-line. Headwinds: $300-350M China export control hit spread across Dec Q and 2026, gross margins guided down 50bps to 62% on mix, foundry/logic revenue mix declining sequentially on China reset. Service growth 16% YoY, DRAM/HBM process control intensity up. Direct, confident Q&A. Not a 5 because Dec Q guide is only modestly up and a meaningful China headwind is now quantified; the bull case is more 2H26 than near-term.

Clear beat-and-raise: Q3 record revenue $737.2M (+10.9% QoQ, +18.9% YoY), EPS $4.73 vs $4.64. CFO explicitly guided enterprise data 30-40% growth in 2026 (weighted to 2H), auto layering design wins through 2027, first BMS robotics design win. Diversified growth across all end-markets. Stock context quip ('900 to 400') shows CEO aware of skepticism but confident numbers will speak. Negatives: gross margin stuck at mid-55% (down from peak), short 3-4 month visibility, CEO repeatedly deflected on near-term forecasting ('we don't predict'), Q1 visibility limited, 2026 enterprise data acceleration weighted to 2H not 1H, guide up only ~1% sequentially for Q4. Hedging Q&A on margins, HVDC/800V timing described as 2027-2028. Solid fundamentals but a deceleration-to-1% QoQ guide right after big 11% Q3 could disappoint momentum buyers near-term.

Exceptional beat-and-raise with strongest forward signals of the group: Q4 record revenue $11.3B (+22% QoQ, +46% YoY), EPS $3.03 vs $2.86, Q1 guide $12.5B record plus GM jumping from 45.7% to 51.5% (+580bps sequentially). HBM revenue ~$2B in Q4 (~$8B run rate), 6 customers, pricing agreements locked for 'vast majority' of HBM3e calendar 2026 supply. Industry DRAM tight, further tightness expected in 2026; they explicitly call out tight industry supply as a multi-year tailwind. DRAM inventory days below target. CMBU GM 59%, CDBU GM up 400bps QoQ, MCBU GM up 12 points. New segment disclosures highlighting profitability. Management tone is direct, specific, with multiple concrete forward catalysts (1-gamma ramp, HBM4 sampling at 2.8TB/s, customized HBM4e with TSMC). Few hedges. This is the cleanest continue-momentum signal in the group.

Mixed signals. Positives: record Q1 FCF $1.2B, EBITDA $2.6B, divestiture program complete ($3.2B proceeds), $1B debt paid down, $755M buybacks, benefiting from gold price surge. Negatives/hedging: no guidance raise (only 'on track'), AISC elevated at $1,651/oz, production is 52% H2-weighted (implying H1 is lower-run-rate), Boddington 53% H2-weighted, Cadia transitioning through lower grades until 2H26, Lihir in lower-grade period 'for next couple of years' until 2028, quarter benefited heavily from gold price rather than operational improvement. Management tone is disciplined and sober but explicitly says 'we still have work to do to improve our margins,' 'we're in an investment cycle,' 'unit costs that are high.' Tariff commentary cautious. Gold-price beta dominates — momentum continuation depends more on gold than on company-specific catalysts. Operationally treading water while cost discipline is called out as still needed.

New $3B buyback authorization through 2028, committed to $1B repurchases annually plus 7-9% dividend growth. Texas segment EBITDA +38% YoY, Smart Home customer growth 9% vs 5-6% target. Direct confident CEO tone. Multiple compounding positive catalysts with clear visibility.
